issue.payload:
Now I have enough to judge. Let me verify the full set of reasons extracted from both files against the comment.

From `route.sh` assignments to `_ROUTE_LOOP_TERMINATED_REASON`: `signal`, `router_budget_exceeded`, `router_config_error`, `done_sentinel`, `router_rate_limited`, `router_timeout`, `no_done_sentinel`.

From `router-rc-classify.sh` `printf -v "$reason_var"` statements: `router_rate_limited`, `router_out_of_turns`, `""` (empty—skipped), `router_timeout`, `router_oom_kill`, `router_config_error`, `router_rc_nonzero`.

Union (non-empty): `done_sentinel`, `no_done_sentinel`, `router_timeout`, `router_rate_limited`, `router_out_of_turns`, `router_oom_kill`, `router_rc_nonzero`, `router_config_error`, `router_budget_exceeded`, `signal` — exactly 10 values.

The comment in `route.sh` now reads: `done_sentinel | no_done_sentinel | router_timeout | router_rate_limited | router_out_of_turns | router_oom_kill | router_rc_nonzero | router_config_error | router_budget_exceeded | signal` — exactly the same 10 values.

---

MET: RQDIFF-1
MET: RQDIFF-2
MET: RQDIFF-3
MET: RQEND-1
MET: RQLOCK-1
MET: RQLOCK-2
MET: RQLOCK-3

UNASKED: summary.sh new elif branch adds a `warn` line not asked for by any requirement | WHY: RQDIFF-1 and RQDIFF-2 require only that `build.discrepancy.detected` is emitted; the warn line is not part of the stated acceptance criteria | QUOTE: plugins/agent/build/lib/summary.sh | warn "build: loop ended on $terminated_reason with 0 files changed" >&2 || true

---

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 1: wrong — the test uses `|| true` after `grep -c`, not `|| echo 0`; `_dslock1_nds="$(grep -c '_ROUTE_LOOP_TERMINATED_REASON="no_done_sentinel"' "$_route_sh" 2>/dev/null || true)"` with the default `${_dslock1_nds:-0}` handling the empty case; the antipattern is absent.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 2: wrong — `git diff 6a07fa8e…HEAD -- tests/unit/route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` produces no output; O4 is unchanged, confirmed by empty diff.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 3: wrong — `scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh` and `tests/unit/router-rc-classify-test.sh` are absent from the diff; no T2 assertions were touched.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 4: wrong — same as finding 2; the diff for `route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` between base and HEAD is empty; O4 is unchanged.

ANSWER lens-security-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses, does not block): wrong — the awk in `route-loop-terminated-reasons-test.sh` already has the dual-exit condition (`in_fn && /^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]*\(\)/` exits on a following function signature, `in_fn && /^}[[:space:]]*$/` exits on a bare closing brace); `_router_rc_classify` in the current file has no column-0 `}` inside its body, so extraction is correct for current code; the finding is a future-robustness concern, not a current defect.

ANSWER lens-red-team-code finding 1 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — `_router_rc_classify` in `scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh` contains no column-0 `}` inside its function body; the awk extracts all seven reason values correctly from current code; the concern is hypothetical refactoring, not a present extraction failure.

ANSWER lens-red-team-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — lines 68–71 of `route-loop-terminated-reasons-test.sh` contain an explicit guard: `if [[ -z "$_required" ]]; then assert_fail "[DSEND-1] GUARD: reason extraction produced a non-empty required set" …; fi`; vacuous pass on empty extraction is blocked.

ANSWER lens-red-team-code finding 3 (opened by review_lenses, does not block): wrong — the hardcoded SHA `6a07fa8e` is used only in DSLOCK-3, whose sole purpose is to verify `route-one-call-per-try-test.sh` was not modified in this worktree; `2>&1 || true` captures any git fatal and makes `_dslock3_diff` non-empty, causing the assertion to fail with a clear message; this is a correct failure mode for a test that checks worktree-specific invariants.

ANSWER lens-correctness-code finding 1 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — same reasoning as red-team finding 1; the current `_router_rc_classify` body has no column-0 `}`, so the extraction is correct; the concern applies only to hypothetical future changes.

ANSWER lens-correctness-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses, does not block): wrong — RQDIFF-3 requires only that "behavior remains as today"; the existing `done_sentinel` path already carries `terminated_reason=$terminated_reason` in the emitted event (unchanged by this diff), and DSDIFF-3 is a guard that the two events still fire; a payload assertion would add test depth beyond what RQDIFF-3 asks.

ANSWER lens-sre-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses, does not block): wrong — scanning all of `route.sh` rather than only `route_to_model_loop`'s body makes the extraction more conservative, not less; the DSEND-1 requirement asks that the comment lists exactly the values the code assigns, and `signal` from `_route_signal_handler` is a value `route_to_model_loop` does reach via its signal handler; the extraction is correct.
